claims.statement: For the original fixed selector F(T,p), the exact identity S(T,p)=Q_p-Q_(p-1) and the rooted component recurrence in the source report are valid for every finite ordinary tree and eligible (T,p). The bounded computations are accurately scoped: all labeled trees through order 8 yield no eligible rows, and the T_m replay covers only m<=8. These facts reduce the target to a fixed marked-rank comparison but do not prove its sign.
claims.scope: Critique of the single source claim U6-MARKED-RECURRENCE-TRANSPORT under the solution contract’s ordinary-tree domain, original distinct leaf tags, fixed F(T,p), and exact eligibility guards; finite computation only at its stated bounds.
claims.reason: retained: the algebra, rooted component decomposition, original support deletions, fixed-selector use, and bounded evidence statements check. In particular each summand is q_v(p)-q_v(p-1), the unique component attachment follows from the tree property, and the delta_v substitution gives the stated bridge. The all-tree census has no eligible rows and the 13 T_m rows are bounded evidence only. No step establishes the universal aggregate marked-rank inequality, and no full eligible positive-sum counterexample is given; proposed status remains open.

limitations: This review verifies the exact reduction and replays the bounded scripts; it does not prove or refute the arbitrary-tree marked-rank comparison.
The all-labeled-tree census through order 8 has no eligible rows; it provides no eligible sign evidence.
The T_m replay is limited to m=1..8 and supplies no family theorem.
